_: THE CAPTAINS' CATALOGUE (K4, docs/SKILLS_AND_CAPTAINS.md §4.1, §4.2, §4.9) — authored. Who the captains ARE is data/officers.json; what a grade, a trait and a language ARE is this file. scripts/build-captains.mjs reads both and generates data/captains.generated.json (every captain's grade, kit of ten traits and languages, and every harbour's language); migration 0156 loads them and scripts/db/world-guard.mjs holds the database to all three files on every apply.
_grades: OWNER O3 (row 61): S 5 slots / 10 traits, A 4 / 8, you get the pattern — B 3 / 6, C 2 / 4. `floor_pct` is DEFAULT D10 / D12: a captain's grade at birth is the highest grade whose floor her job value reaches (C 4-5 %, B 5.5-6.5 %, A 7-8 %, S 8.5-9 %), and a promotion (K8) lifts every trait to at least the new floor. A grade above S costs one row ("for now").
_kit: DEFAULT D15: every captain carries TEN ordered traits — her job first at her own value, then up to `same_focus` more of her job's focus, then the rest, each at `extra_pct` % of her job's value (rounded to 0.1). The order after the first is a pure function of her code (md5), so the kit is the same on every build.
_foci: Origin's three foci [UWO §3.2]. The word is what the player reads (Codex filter Role, the trait card).
_promotion: DEFAULT D12 (§4.6): promotion C → B → A → S needs her level in her job's focus (promote_level of the grade she rises to) and promote_items of her focus's item, spent from storage at the port where her ship is docked. The items are the SAME for every captain (never one per captain): one per `points` your fleets earn in that track. Exploration and Combat: 100 points (a Sea Chart ≈ 100,000 miles). Trading: MEASURED (K8, 2026-10-18, production read-only): the merchants — the only sample large enough, the one human sailor having 6,478 miles — turned over 61,712,599 coin across 12,732,386 miles, 4.85 coin a mile, so 100,000 miles ≈ 485,000 coin ≈ 4,850 trading points (100 coin = 1 point): a Trade Seal takes about as long as a Sea Chart.

promotion_items.name: Sea Chart
promotion_items.note: A chart of waters your fleets have sailed: what promotes an exploration captain.

promotion_items.name: Trade Seal
promotion_items.note: A seal of trade your fleets have made: what promotes a trading captain.

promotion_items.name: Battle Honour
promotion_items.note: An honour for pirates your fleets have seen off: what promotes a combat captain.

_effects: What a trait does, by effect (§4.2, §5). `scope` fleet = every seated captain of the fleet adds up; ship = only the ship she sits on (K5). `live` = a rule reads it TODAY while crew_bite is off: the four effects public.fleet_officer_bonus has always served (speed, cargo space, spread, crew saved) — and only for a captain's job (her first trait). `words` is the line the trait card prints ({pct}, {goods}); `waits` is the sentence printed when the trait does not work for this captain yet. `reader` names the ONE rule that will read it. `cap_pct` (K5) is the most a fleet can gain from that effect — read by public.crew_pct, the one reader, which also retired the old `officer_bonus_cap_pct` knob (the four live effects carry its 25). category_spread's cap is per goods category.
_traits: The 25 traits (§4.2): the four live jobs (O6), Pilot (O6: kinder weather), Provisioner (D15), one trader per goods category (O5, the owner's 17 categories of row 70: jewellery → Gem trader, meat → Food trader) and the two combat jobs (O5: long range, close). `ord` is the catalogue order; `goods` is data/goods.json's category code a trader works on, `goods_word` how the card names it. A trait may carry two effects (the surgeon). Every trait is some captain's job (at least two captains each, D15).
_cabins: DEFAULT D9 (§4.3): seat 1 of every ship is the Captain's cabin, where every trait works at 100 %. The other seats (class_cabins: 3-8 per hull) are typed, in turn, starting with the hull's own role (`rotation`, by class_profile.role): a trait of the cabin's focus works at 100 %, any other at `cabin_off_focus_pct` % (the knob, 50 — Origin's official figure). Captains are seated, moved and put ashore only while the ship is in port; no ship needs a captain to sail.
_languages: DEFAULT D14 (§4.9): twenty languages, one for each people the map has. A language is NEVER a gate. A harbour's language: a named exception (`by_port`), else its founding nation's (`by_nation`), else its culture's (`by_culture`), else — only for a Latin harbour of no nation, since there is no single Latin language — its country's (`by_country`); a harbour none of the four names fails the generator rather than being guessed. A captain speaks her home's language; an A captain one more and an S captain two more, the languages most spoken in her home region first.
_by_port: Feodosia (Kaffa) was an Ottoman port from 1475; the data gives it no nation, and its culture would say Arabic.
